case_name: Thammu Panduranga Rao and another v State of Andhra Pradesh
respondent:
State of Andhra Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

26 April 2013
Cr.A. No. 1132 of 2009
The Judgment was delivered by : M. Y. Eqbal, J.
1. The present appeal by special leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 9th October, 2007 passed by the High Court of Judicature of Andhra Pradesh partly allowing Criminal Appeal No. 1187 of 2002 filed by the appellants herein (accused Nos. 1 and 2) by inter alia modifying the conviction of accused Nos. 1 and 2 for the offence u/s. 304 IPC into conviction for the offence u/s. 304(2) IPC and reducing the sentence of rigorous imprisonment of 10 years to three years in respect of both the accused and the sentence of rigorous imprisonment of four years for the offence u/s. 325 IPC in respect of accused No. 2 to one year.

facts: The case of the prosecution which led to the conviction of accused Nos. 1 and 2 is that the deceased Boddu Maraiah and accused No. 2 were having prior disputes between them.

On 2.11.1998 at about 5.30 p.m., while accused Nos. 1 to 5 (A-1 to A-5) were returning to their village after finishing their fishing work and when they reached near the cattle shed of the deceased, they heard PW-2 (wife of deceased) abusing her cattle sarcastically.

The trial court on consideration of testimony of the witnesses held that a case has been made out against A-1 and A-2 (appellants herein) finding them guilty for the offences under Sections 304/34, 324/34 and 325 IPC.
A-3 had died on 5.12.1998 due to ill health while under judicial custody.
issues: Whether the accused intended to kill the deceased?
Whether the cumulative effect of the injuries led to the death of the deceased?
Whether the accused used sharp edged weapons to kill the deceased?
petitioner_arguments: Their guilt was not proved beyond all reasonable doubt.
Their conviction and sentence ought to be set aside.
respondent_arguments: The lower court gave sufficient reasons as to why the respective accused were convicted for the offences under various Sections of IPC.
There was no ground to interfere with the conviction of the accused for the offences under Sections 304, 325 and 323 IPC.
court_reasoning: It cannot be held that they have committed the offence u/s 302 r/w s. 34 IPC, but they have committed an offence punishable u/s 304 r/w s. 34 IPC, in other words culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

The cumulative effect of the injuries led to the death of the deceased and A-1 being the person who participated in the commission of the offence was also having common intention to attack the deceased.
holding: The appeal of A-1 and A-2 (appellants herein) was partly allowed by the High Court as mentioned hereinbefore.
